title: Sypris Wins Expanded Follow-On Award for Deep Space Program
summary: The Investor Relations website contains information about Sypris Solutions, Inc.'s business for stockholders, potential investors, and financial analysts.
body_text: PDF Version Electronic Assemblies for Orion Spacecraft Sensor Systems TAMPA, Fla.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Jan. 13, 2026-- Sypris Electronics, LLC, a subsidiary of Sypris Solutions, Inc. (Nasdaq/GM: SYPR), announced today that it has received an expanded follow-on award from a leading U.S. aerospace and defense contractor to produce and test circuit card assemblies for use in Orion spacecraft supporting the missions of NASA’s Artemis program. Production is scheduled to begin in 2026. Financial terms were not disclosed. The Orion spacecraft is designed to serve as the primary exploration vehicle for the Artemis program, enabling crewed missions to destinations such as the moon, while also functioning as a small, multi-purpose space station to support continued scientific research and technology development in preparation for establishing a sustained human presence in deep space. The critical electronic assemblies to be produced by Sypris Electronics will be embedded within the Orion spacecraft and support space-grade sensor systems, including navigation, altitude determination and environmental monitoring, as well as crew safety functions essential to mission success. “We are pleased to have this important opportunity to expand our involvement with the Orion spacecraft and the Artemis program,” said Mike Sedgwick, Vice President and General Manager of Sypris Electronics. “Our backlog on this program now extends through 2027, providing production continuity and support for NASA’s efforts to establish a sustained human presence in deep space through the timely delivery of this critical technology.” Sypris Electronics is a trusted provider of complex, mission-critical electronic solutions for customers in the Defense, Space, Deep Sea Communications and Industrial sectors. With over 50 years of experience, the Company specializes in manufacturing electronics for high-cost-of-failure applications. For more information, visit www.sypriselectronics.com . body_text: View All News Timberland Bancorp Reports First Fiscal Quarter Net Income of $8.2 Million January 26, 2026 EPS Increases 21% to $1.04 from $0.86 for the Comparable Quarter One Year Ago Quarterly Return on Average Assets of 1.60% Quarterly Return on Average Equity of 12.33% Quarterly Net Interest Margin Increases to 3.85% Announces a 4% Increase in the Quarterly Cash Dividend HOQUIAM, Wash., Jan. 26, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Timberland Bancorp, Inc. (NASDAQ: TSBK) (“Timberland” or “the Company”), the holding company for Timberland Bank (the “Bank”), today reported net income of $8.22 million, or $1.04 per diluted common share for the quarter ended December 31, 2025. This compares to net income of $6.86 million, or $0.86 per diluted common share for the comparable quarter one year ago, and $8.45 million, or $1.07 per diluted common share, for the preceding quarter. “Timberland delivered strong profitability this quarter, demonstrating the fundamental strength and resilience of our business model,” stated Dean Brydon, Chief Executive Officer. “In the first quarter, net income increased 20% from a year ago, with earnings per share up 21%, reflecting our disciplined approach to growth and operation efficiency. Compared to the prior quarter, net income was down 3%, largely due to a $1.04 million bank owned life insurance (“BOLI”) benefit claim realized during the prior quarter. However, when adjusted for the one-time BOLI impact, net income and earnings per share increased by approximately 11% over the prior quarter.” “As a result of Timberland’s strong earnings and capital position, our Board of Directors announced a 4% increase to the quarterly cash dividend to shareholders to $0.29 per share, payable on February 27, 2026, to shareholders of record on February 13, 2026,” stated Jonathan Fischer, President and Chief Operating Officer. “This represents the 53rd consecutive quarter Timberland will have paid a cash dividend and demonstrates the Board’s continued confidence in our long-term outlook.” “Our strong quarterly results reflect several positive trends across our business,” said Marci Basich, Chief Financial Officer. “We continued to see expansion in our net interest margin, which increased three basis points from the prior quarter and 21 basis points year-over-year. The current quarter included additional non-accrual interest and late fees collected, which increased the margin by approximately 6 basis points. Our balance sheet positioning and proactive deposit pricing strategies successfully offset the headwinds from recent Federal Reserve rate cuts and the resulting lower rate environment. Total deposits decreased 1% from the prior quarter and increased 5% year-over-year, with a portion of the quarterly decrease due to a reduction in brokered deposits. Going forward, our focus remains on preserving a diversified funding mix and sustaining stable margin performance.” “We're taking a disciplined approach to balance sheet expansion in the current environment, prioritizing quality and returns over volume,” Brydon continued. “Net loans decreased slightly during the quarter primarily due to an increase in loan payoffs. Credit quality remains an area we continue to monitor closely, though performance across the portfolio remains solid with net recoveries of $18,000 for the quarter. The non-performing assets (“NPA”) ratio remained flat at 0.23% at December 31, 2025, compared to the prior quarter end, and loans graded “Substandard” decreased significantly during the period. We remain confident in the overall health of our loan portfolio and our disciplined approach to credit risk management.” “We are pleased to announce that we officially opened our new full-service branch in University Place on January 12, 2026. University Place is near Tacoma, WA and the new branch is located between our Gig Harbor and Tacoma branches. This strategic expansion positions us to deepen our presence in a dynamic market and build stronger commercial banking relationships with the businesses driving growth in this community,” said Fischer. Earnings and Balance Sheet Highlights (at or for the periods ended December 31, 2025, compared to December 31, 2024, or September 30, 2025): Earnings Highlights: EPS increased 21% to $1.04 for the current quarter from $0.86 for the comparable quarter one year ago and decreased 3% from $1.07 for the preceding quarter; Net income increased 20% to $8.22 million for the current quarter from $6.86 million for the comparable quarter one year ago and decreased 3% from $8.45 million for the preceding quarter (which included a $1.04 million BOLI benefit claim); Return on average equity (“ROE”) and return on average assets (“ROA”) for the current quarter were 12.33% and 1.60%, respectively; Net interest margin (“NIM”) for the current quarter increased to 3.85% from 3.82% for the preceding quarter and 3.64% for the comparable quarter one year ago; and The efficiency ratio for the current quarter improved to 52.65% from 53.18% for the preceding quarter and 56.27% for the comparable quarter one year ago. Balance Sheet Highlights: Total assets decreased slightly, less than 1%, from the prior quarter and increased 5% year-over-year; Net loans receivable decreased slightly, less than 1% from the prior quarter and increased 3% year-over-year; Total deposits decreased 1% from the prior quarter and increased 5% year-over-year; Total shareholders’ equity increased 2% from the prior quarter and increased 8% year-over-year; 29,303 shares of common stock were repurchased during the current quarter for $1.01 million; Non-performing assets to total assets ratio was 0.23% at December 31, 2025, compared to 0.23% at September 30, 2025, and 0.16% at December 31, 2024; Book and tangible book (non-GAAP) values per common share increased to $34.06 and $32.11 respectively, at December 31, 2025; and Liquidity (both on-balance sheet and off-balance sheet) remained strong at December 31, 2025, with only $20 million in borrowings and additional secured borrowing line capacity of $761 million available through the Federal Home Loan Bank (“FHLB”) and the Federal Reserve. Operating Results Operating revenue (net interest income before the provision for credit losses plus non-interest income) for the current quarter decreased 3% to $21.71 million from $22.49 million for the preceding quarter and increased 10% from $19.67 million for the comparable quarter one year ago. The decrease in operating revenue compared to the preceding quarter was primarily due to a decrease in non-interest income, and to a lesser extent, a decrease in interest income from investment securities, which was partially offset by an increase in interest income on loans receivable and on interest bearing deposits in banks. Non-interest income was higher in the quarter ended September 30, 2025, primarily due to a $1.04 million BOLI death benefit claim recorded during the quarter. Net interest income increased $554,000, or 3%, to $18.95 million for the current quarter from $18.40 million for the preceding quarter and increased $1.98 million, or 12%, from $16.97 million for the comparable quarter one year ago. The increase in net interest income compared to the preceding quarter was primarily due to a $43.49 million increase in the average balance of total interest-earning assets and a five-basis point decrease in the weighted average cost of interest-bearing liabilities. These increases were partially offset by a $36.02 million increase in the average balance of interest-bearing liabilities and a one-basis point decrease in the weighted average yield of interest-bearing assets. Timberland’s NIM for the current quarter improved to 3.85% from 3.82% for the preceding quarter and 3.64% for the comparable quarter one year ago. The NIM for the current quarter was increased by approximately six basis points due to the collection of $282,000 in pre-payment penalties, non-accrual interest, and late fees, and the accretion of $9,000 of the fair value discount on acquired loans. The NIM for the preceding quarter was increased by approximately two basis points due to the collection of $102,000 in pre-payment penalties, non-accrual interest, and late fees, and the accretion of $11,000 of the fair value discount on acquired loans. The NIM for the comparable quarter one year ago was increased by approximately three basis points due to the collection of $115,000 in pre-payment penalties, non-accrual interest, and late fees, and the accretion of $8,000 of the fair value discount on acquired loans. Non-interest income decreased $1.33 million, or 32%, to $2.76 million for the current quarter from $4.09 million for the preceding quarter and increased $67,000, or 2%, from $2.70 million for the comparable quarter one year ago. The decrease in non-interest income compared to the preceding quarter was primarily due to a decrease in BOLI net income (from a $1.04 million death benefit claim) and, to a lesser extent, smaller decreases in several other categories. Total operating (non-interest) expenses for the current quarter decreased $528,000, or 4%, to $11.43 million from $11.96 million for the preceding quarter and increased $364,000, or 3%, from $11.07 million for the comparable quarter one year ago. The decrease in operating expenses compared to the preceding quarter was primarily due to decreases in professional fees, loan administration and foreclosure, technology and communications, premises and fixed assets, and several expense recoveries on items in the other, net category. These decreases were partially offset by an increase in salary and employee benefits expense and smaller increases in several other expense categories. The efficiency ratio for the current quarter improved to 52.65% from 53.18% for the preceding quarter and 56.27% for the comparable quarter one year ago. The provision for income taxes for the current quarter increased $240,000, or 13%, to $2.10 million from $1.86 million for the preceding quarter, primarily due to higher taxable income. Timberland’s effective income tax rate was 20.4% for the quarter ended December 31, 2025, compared to 18.1% for the quarter ended September 30, 2025, and 20.0% for the quarter ended December 31, 2024. The lower effective income tax rate for the September 30, 2025 quarter was primarily due to a higher percentage of non-taxable income as a result of a BOLI benefit claim. Balance Sheet Management Total assets decreased $6.65 million, or less than 1%, during the quarter to $2.01 billion at December 31, 2025, from $2.01 billion at September 30, 2025, and increased $96.65 million, or 5%, from $1.91 billion one year ago. Liquidity Timberland has continued to maintain a strong liquidity position, both on-balance sheet and off-balance sheet. Liquidity, as measured by the sum of cash and cash equivalents, CDs held for investment, and available for sale investment securities, was 18.9% of total liabilities at December 31, 2025, compared to 18.8% at September 30, 2025, and 15.0% one year ago. Timberland also had secured borrowing line capacity of $761 million available through the FHLB and the Federal Reserve at December 31, 2025. With a strong and diversified deposit base, only 18% of Timberland’s deposits were uninsured or uncollateralized at December 31, 2025. (Note: This calculation excludes public deposits that are fully collateralized.) The decrease during the quarter was primarily due to an $18.16 million decrease in construction loans, a $2.41 million decrease in land loans and smaller decreases in several other loan categories. body_text: Jan. 23, 2026 By Constantine “Kosta” Kapatos, Elbit America Vice President of Business Development for Warfighter Systems For generations, night vision capability has delivered a decisive tactical advantage to the United States and its allied forces. As the battlefield has evolved, so has the technology behind it. Today’s missions demand more than visibility. They demand confidence in the most uncertain, low-light conditions to increase a warfighter’s survivability and lethality. That’s where Elbit America’s Gen 3 image intensifier technology makes the difference. The modern battlefield is anything but predictable. Warfighters move from heavy canopy to open terrain, from urban glow to pure starlight, often in a single operation. In these scenarios, warfighters need a dependable solution that allows them to optimally sense their changing surroundings. Gen 3 image intensifier tubes are built for that reality. From the start of their service life – and throughout it – Gen 3 tubes outperform Gen 2 in the conditions that matter most: extreme low light. Gen 3 image intensifier tubes' superiority means they’re not produced by just anyone. They’re exclusive. The “Gen 3” designation is not simply a marketing moniker; it’s an official designation based on U.S. military specifications defined by the U.S. Army Command, Control, Communications, Computers, Cyber, Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance ( C5ISR) Center . Elbit America tubes have earned this designation, and the company is one of only two U.S. manufacturers who produce Gen 3 tubes. Why Gen 3 Performs Where Gen 2 Fades The difference begins at the photocathode. Gen 3 uses gallium arsenide (GaAs), delivering significantly higher sensitivity and luminance gain, especially in the visible and near-infrared wavelengths that dominate true nighttime environments. The result is greater recognition range, sharper imagery, and usable vision in near-total darkness. These are conditions where Gen 2 systems struggle or stop working altogether. In well-lit or urban environments, the difference may appear subtle. But in the darkest of conditions, where night vision is needed most, Gen 3 is the only technology that consistently delivers operational capability. Performance That Lasts Gen 3 doesn’t just perform better; it performs longer and more consistently over time than Gen 2. The addition of a protective ion barrier film dramatically increases reliability and service life, enabling 10,000+ hours of operational use under stringent U.S. military specification standards. When tested to the same standards, Gen 2 tubes don’t compare as they’re weaker from the start. But also, their performance degrades quickly and then drops over time – rendering them nearly useless for challenging real-world operating conditions after just two years. Meanwhile, a Gen 3 image intensifier tube executes with superior performance, reliability, and recognition range after multiple years of service life, with only the slightest of degradation over time. Simply put: one Gen 3 image intensifier tube can replace four to five Gen 2 image intensifier tubes over time. That means less downtime, fewer replacements, and lower total lifecycle cost without sacrificing performance as the system ages. Marketing Buzz Vs. Reality Don’t be fooled! The U.S. military does not offer a current Gen 4 designation for image intensification tubes, and they’re creating the standard for night vision globally. Those who tout “4G” or “4th Gen capability” are clever marketers, simply promoting advancements made to their inferior Gen 2 technology. They’re not delivering the incomparable clarity, reliability, and service life of an Elbit America Gen 3 image intensifier tube. Our Gen 3 tubes continue to set the standard. body_text: Shopify Conversion Rate Optimization The Ultimate Guide Mariam Ahmed Co-founder & CTO · January 13, 2026 Shopify conversion rate optimisation isn’t some dark art. It’s simply the process of methodically improving your online store to increase the percentage of visitors who buy something. It involves getting inside your customers’ heads, analysing their behaviour, finding the spots where they get stuck or frustrated, and then making smart changes—from small design tweaks to a complete checkout overhaul—to make buying from you easier and more appealing. The goal is simple: turn more of your existing traffic into paying customers. Establishing Your Shopify Conversion Baseline Before you can start improving anything, you have to know where you stand. Guesswork is the enemy of effective CRO; data is your only reliable friend. Building a clear, honest, and data-backed baseline isn’t just a preliminary step—it’s the foundation for your entire optimisation strategy. Without it, you’re just flying blind, unable to measure if your hard work is actually making a difference. Your first move should be to get all your data talking to each other. While Shopify Analytics gives you a decent overview, pairing it with Google Analytics 4 (GA4) provides a much richer, more granular picture of user behaviour. This dual-platform approach lets you cross-reference everything, ensuring accuracy and uncovering insights that one tool alone would almost certainly miss. For a full breakdown of strategies, our guide on Shopify Conversion Rate Optimization is a great place to start. What Is a Good Conversion Rate? It’s the million-dollar question: “What’s a good conversion rate?” Honestly, the answer is… it depends. While global benchmarks are interesting, a “good” rate is hyper-specific to your niche, price point, and who you’re selling to. A UK-based fashion brand will have a completely different performance standard than a high-end electronics store. To set goals that actually make sense, you need to look at industry-specific data. It’s a useful exercise to see how your store stacks up against others in your sector. Here’s a look at some UK Shopify benchmarks to give you some context. Industry Sector Average Conversion Rate Fashion & Apparel 1.8% Health & Beauty 2.9% Home & Garden 1.6% Food & Drink 2.5% Electronics 1.2% These numbers help frame your performance, but remember they are just averages. Your own historical data is the most important benchmark you have. In the UK, Shopify has a massive 20% market share among e-commerce platforms, so there’s a huge amount of data out there. While a broad survey pegs the average Shopify conversion rate at 1.4% , the top-performing UK stores consistently hit 3.2% or higher , putting them in the top 20% globally. Reaching an impressive 4.7% lands a store in the elite top 10%. This tells you one thing very clearly: aiming for “average” is aiming too low. The real opportunity is in understanding what the top performers are doing and setting your sights on joining them. Finding Your True Performance Level With your analytics connected, it’s time to establish your baseline conversion rate over a meaningful period. I always recommend looking at the last 90 days —it’s long enough to smooth out any weird spikes from sales or holidays. But don’t just stop at the overall store conversion rate. That number hides the real story. You need to dig deeper. Conversion Rate by Traffic Source: Are visitors from organic search converting better than your social media ads? This tells you where your best customers are coming from. Conversion Rate by Device: How does mobile stack up against desktop? A big gap here is a massive red flag, usually pointing to a clunky mobile experience. Add to Cart Rate: What percentage of people actually add a product to their cart? If this is low, your product pages or pricing might be the problem. Checkout Abandonment Rate: How many people start checking out but never finish? This is one of the most critical friction points to fix. By segmenting your conversion data, you move from a vague, store-wide number to a precise map of strengths and weaknesses. This detailed analysis reveals exactly where you should focus your optimisation efforts for the greatest impact. Once you have this detailed baseline, you can set realistic, incremental goals. Forget about trying to double your conversion rate overnight. Instead, focus on improving one metric at a time. Maybe you aim to increase your mobile conversion rate by 10% next quarter. This targeted approach is far more effective and sustainable. To learn more about this process, you can explore our guide on how to analyse Shopify data to boost ecommerce growth . Getting this data-driven foundation right is the first real step in any successful CRO journey. Finding and Fixing Hidden Conversion Killers Right, you’ve got your baseline sorted. Now the real detective work begins. Your store’s analytics are packed with clues explaining why people leave without buying. The goal isn’t just spotting problems, but getting to the why behind the numbers. It’s about finding those subtle friction points that are silently killing your sales. Think of your customer journey like a relay race. Each stage—from homepage to product page, to the cart, and through checkout—is a crucial handoff. A dropped baton at any point means a lost sale. To get Shopify CRO right, you need to become an expert at spotting where those drops happen. Uncovering Friction with Behavioural Analytics The numbers from Shopify Analytics or GA4 tell you what is happening—for example, a 50% drop-off on product pages. But the real gold is in the qualitative data that tells you why . This is where behavioural analytics tools are indispensable; they’re your window into the actual user experience. Tools like Hotjar or Microsoft Clarity are brilliant for this diagnostic phase. They offer two features you absolutely need: Heatmaps: These are visual overlays showing exactly where users click, move their mouse, and how far they scroll. Are they trying to click on something that isn’t a link? Are they completely missing your main call-to-action? You’ll see it instantly. Session Recordings: Watching anonymised recordings of real user sessions is like looking over their shoulder. You can witness their confusion firsthand as they wrestle with a clunky navigation menu or rage-click a broken button. These tools bridge the gap between abstract numbers and human behaviour. A high bounce rate is just a statistic; watching five users in a row fail to find the size chart is a clear, actionable problem you can fix immediately. Prioritising Your Hit List Once you start digging, you’ll probably uncover a dozen potential issues. The trick is to avoid getting bogged down and, instead, create a prioritised hit list. You need to focus on the friction points with the biggest potential impact on your revenue. Ask yourself these questions to sort out your priorities: Where’s the biggest drop-off happening? If 70% of users who add to cart never even start the checkout, that’s a much bigger fire to put out than a minor typo on your ‘About Us’ page. How many users are affected? A bug hitting every mobile user is a higher priority than one impacting a tiny segment on an old browser. How hard is the fix? Sometimes, a simple copy change or tweaking a theme setting can deliver a big win with minimal effort. Tackle these “quick wins” first to build momentum. One of the most stubborn conversion killers for Shopify stores is the abandoned cart. Understanding the most effective strategies to reduce cart abandonment is absolutely crucial. Surprise shipping costs discovered at the last minute are a classic culprit. The UK Mobile Challenge For UK-based Shopify merchants, the data points to a very specific area of concern. Industry benchmarks show massive differences between categories: general apparel might convert at 2% , while luxury handbags lag at a tiny 0.3% . Knowing these nuances is vital. But the most glaring friction point is almost always the mobile experience. While UK mobile e-commerce conversion rates average a respectable 2.89% , cart abandonment on mobile devices soars to an eye-watering 85.65% , compared to 73.76% on desktop. This huge gap points directly to clunky mobile checkouts, fiddly forms, and payment friction as major conversion blockers. You can find more details in these UK-specific CRO statistics on Shopify.com . This data isn’t just interesting—it’s a direct instruction. If your UK-based store isn’t obsessively optimised for a seamless, one-click mobile checkout, you are leaving an enormous amount of money on the table. By systematically identifying these friction points—from confusing navigation witnessed in session recordings to checkout abandonment triggered by unexpected costs—you transform guesswork into a data-driven plan of attack. Implementing High-Impact Store Optimisations Okay, you’ve done the hard work of digging through your data and now you have a prioritised list of friction points. It’s time to roll up your sleeves and turn those insights into tangible improvements that actually move the needle on your conversion rate. The key here isn’t to tear down your whole store and start again. That’s a recipe for chaos. The smart approach is to systematically knock down the highest-impact issues you’ve uncovered one by one. This is about more than just changing a button colour; it’s about fundamentally improving your customer’s journey. We’ll focus on the areas that consistently deliver the biggest wins: product pages that sell, navigation that guides, and a checkout that’s as smooth as silk. Revitalise Your Product Pages Your product page is the final sales pitch. It’s where a browser becomes a buyer, so it needs to be compelling, trustworthy, and crystal clear. I see so many stores fall flat here with generic descriptions and mediocre images, which just plants seeds of doubt and kills momentum. To truly nail Shopify conversion rate optimisation , your product pages must answer every question a customer might have before they even think to ask it. Compelling Imagery and Video: Don’t just show the product; showcase it. Get high-resolution photos from every angle, add some in-context lifestyle shots, and include close-ups of key details. A short video of the product in action can be a game-changer, helping customers really visualise it in their own lives. Benefit-Driven Descriptions: Stop listing features and start explaining benefits. Instead of “100% organic cotton,” try “Crafted from ultra-soft, breathable organic cotton for all-day comfort.” You’re connecting the dots for the customer, linking your product directly to their needs and wants. Powerful Social Proof: Nothing builds trust faster than seeing that other people have bought—and loved—your product. Display star ratings and written reviews prominently. Go a step further and pull in user-generated content (UGC) by showcasing customer photos from Instagram. That real-world validation is often the final nudge a hesitant shopper needs. Streamline Navigation and Search If people can’t find what they’re looking for in seconds, they’re gone. A confusing navigation menu or a clunky search function are absolute conversion killers. Your only goal here is to make product discovery completely effortless. A clean, logical menu is non-negotiable. Use simple, clear category names that your customers would actually search for. If you have a massive catalogue, a well-designed “mega menu” can display subcategories without overwhelming the user. A classic mistake, especially on mobile, is hiding the search bar behind a tiny magnifying glass icon. Make the search bar prominent and sticky at the top of the page. It encourages use and dramatically cuts down on frustration for shoppers who know exactly what they want. Think about the hint text, too. Instead of a bland “Search,” try something more inviting like, “What are you looking for?” It’s a tiny tweak that makes the whole experience feel more personal. Perfect the Checkout Experience The checkout is the final hurdle, and it’s where an astonishing number of sales are lost. Your primary objective is to eliminate every single point of friction, doubt, or surprise. Scrutinise every field, every step, every click. By 2024 , with over 209,000 Shopify stores in the United Kingdom, the data on what works is clearer than ever. While the average conversion rate hovers around a paltry 1.4% , top-tier UK merchants consistently hit over 3.2% . A huge driver for this is their adoption of accelerated checkouts like Shop Pay. In fact, studies show Shop Pay can produce 50% higher conversions than a standard guest checkout. You can dig into more of these impactful Shopify statistics and trends yourself. This data gives us a clear directive for optimising the checkout. Key Checkout Optimisations Simplify Your Forms: Only ask for the absolute bare minimum. Every extra field is another reason for someone to abandon their cart. Use address autocomplete to reduce typing and prevent errors. Offer Trusted Payment Options: Build instant trust by displaying logos for Visa, Mastercard, and PayPal. But crucially, you must enable accelerated options like Shop Pay, Apple Pay, and Google Pay. These let returning customers check out in seconds, completely bypassing the tedious manual entry of their details. Be Transparent with Costs: Unexpected shipping costs are the number one reason for cart abandonment. Show your shipping fees as early as you can—ideally on the product page or in the cart, not as a nasty surprise at the final step. If you offer free shipping over a certain threshold, shout about it across the entire site. By focusing your first wave of effort on these three core areas—product pages, navigation, and checkout—you’ll be tackling the most common and damaging friction points. Each improvement, backed by the data you’ve gathered, builds a smoother, more trustworthy experience that naturally leads to a higher conversion rate. Using Personalisation to Drive More Sales A generic, one-size-fits-all shopping experience is a guaranteed way to leave money on the table. Today’s customers don’t just appreciate a tailored journey; they expect it. By using the customer data you already have, you can move beyond broad-strokes marketing and create a personalised experience that speaks directly to each individual, which is a surefire way to lift your Shopify conversion rate. This isn’t about getting tangled up in complex algorithms. It starts with smart, practical applications of what you know about your visitors. Dynamic product recommendations are a powerful place to begin. Instead of showing everyone your bestsellers, you can display products based on what a user is looking at right now . Someone browsing running shoes should see recommendations for performance socks and hydration packs, not winter coats. That level of relevance makes shoppers feel understood. It transforms your store from a simple catalogue into a helpful personal shopper, fundamentally shifting the customer relationship, building trust, and encouraging them to explore more of what you offer. Tailoring Offers and Incentives Strategic offers are a cornerstone of Shopify conversion rate optimisation, but it’s a delicate balance. Slapping constant, store-wide discounts on everything can devalue your brand and train customers to just wait for a sale. The key is to be surgical with your incentives, presenting the right offer to the right person at the perfect moment. This is where your data becomes your best friend. Instead of blasting everyone with a 10% off coupon, you can create far more nuanced and effective offers: Free Shipping Thresholds: This is a classic for a reason. Clearly communicating “You’re only £15 away from free shipping!” is an incredibly powerful motivator for increasing average order value. Smart Product Bundles: Group complementary items together at a slight discount. If a customer is buying a coffee machine, offering a bundle with filters and your most popular beans is a natural upsell that feels helpful, not pushy. Limited-Time Offers: Create genuine urgency with a special deal that actually expires. This is particularly effective for recovering abandoned carts and nudging hesitant buyers over the finish line. The most effective offers aren’t just about the price cut; they’re about value and timing. A well-placed bundle or a timely free shipping reminder often outperforms a simple percentage discount because it aligns perfectly with what the customer is trying to do in that moment. Automating Personalisation with Email Flows Email remains one of the most potent channels for personalised communication. Automated flows, triggered by specific customer actions, let you deliver hyper-relevant messages at scale without lifting a finger. For any Shopify store, the abandoned cart email is the most critical flow to get right. A generic “You left something behind” email is better than nothing, but a personalised one is exponentially more powerful. Imagine an email that doesn’t just show the exact product left in the cart, but also includes customer reviews for that item and suggests a few closely related alternatives. This transforms a simple reminder into a helpful, persuasive piece of marketing that genuinely re-engages the customer’s interest. Beyond abandoned carts, you should have flows for new subscribers, post-purchase follow-ups, and win-back campaigns for lapsed customers. For Shopify stores using Klaviyo , these automated flows are essential for nurturing customer relationships. For those looking to dive deeper, our guide on how to improve customer retention with Klaviyo and Shopify integrations offers advanced strategies. Each personalised touchpoint strengthens the customer bond, making them more likely to convert not just once, but repeatedly. By using your data to create these tailored experiences, you turn casual browsers into loyal, high-value customers. Creating a System for Testing and Measurement Improving your Shopify conversion rate isn’t about making a few tweaks and hoping for the best. That’s just guesswork. Real growth comes from a disciplined, continuous cycle: form an educated guess, test it in a controlled way, and measure the real-world impact. Without a reliable system for testing, you’re flying blind, unable to tell if a sales lift came from your changes or just random luck. This is where the principles of experimentation come in. The goal is to move from “I think this will work” to “I know this works because the data proves it.” This disciplined approach ensures every change you make is a step forward, building on proven successes rather than gut feelings. It’s how you turn your Shopify store into a well-oiled conversion machine, one validated improvement at a time. The Foundation of A/B Testing At the heart of any solid measurement system is A/B testing , also known as split testing. It’s a beautifully simple concept: you show two different versions of a webpage to two similar groups of visitors at the same time. One group (the control) sees the original page, while the other (the variant) sees your new version. By comparing how each group behaves, you can determine with statistical confidence whether your change had a positive, negative, or negligible effect. It strips all the guesswork out of the process. For instance, you could test things like: A new product page headline: Does a headline focused on benefits get more “Add to Cart” clicks than one that just lists features? A different call-to-action button colour: Does a green “Buy Now” button actually convert better than your original blue one? A simplified checkout process: If we remove that one optional field, does it cut down on checkout abandonment? The rigour of A/B testing is what separates professional Shopify conversion rate optimisation from amateur tinkering. It gives you definitive proof of what really moves the needle. Running a Meaningful Experiment A successful test is so much more than just launching two versions of a page. To get results you can trust, you need a clear process, and it all starts with a strong, measurable hypothesis. A good hypothesis follows a simple structure: “If I make [this specific change], then [this specific outcome] will happen, because [this reason].” For example: “If we add customer reviews directly below the ‘Add to Cart’ button, then the conversion rate will increase, because it will build trust right at the moment of decision.” Next, you need to define your key performance indicators (KPIs). The main goal is often the overall conversion rate, but it’s a huge mistake to ignore secondary metrics. Keep an eye on things like average order value, add-to-cart rate, or even time on page. These help you understand the full story behind your change. A change might slightly decrease your conversion rate but significantly increase your average order value, resulting in a net positive for your business. Without tracking multiple KPIs, you could mistakenly label a profitable experiment as a failure. This process illustrates how customer behaviour can lead to personalised recommendations and, ultimately, a tailored offer. The journey shows that by tracking user actions, you can build a smarter, more responsive shopping experience. Documenting and Learning from Every Test Finally, one of the most overlooked but critical parts of a testing system is documentation. Every single experiment—whether it wins, loses, or is a complete wash—is a learning opportunity. You have to create a central library where you record every detail. Your experiment log should include, at a minimum: The Hypothesis: What did you believe would happen and why? The Variants: A clear description or screenshot of the changes. The Results: Hard data on all the KPIs you tracked, including statistical significance. The Conclusion: What was the final outcome and what did you learn from it? This internal knowledge base becomes an invaluable asset over time. It stops your team from re-testing the same failed ideas six months down the line and gives you a wealth of insights that fuel smarter hypotheses for future experiments. You can learn more about turning your data into clear guidance by exploring our guide on getting actionable insights from your Shopify sales data . Building this system is what transforms CRO from a series of random tactics into a strategic, reliable growth engine for your business. Shopify Conversion Rate Optimisation FAQs When you start digging into Shopify conversion rate optimisation, a few key questions always bubble to the surface. It doesn’t matter if you’re just starting out or fine-tuning a strategy you’ve had for years—getting solid answers to the common sticking points helps you focus your energy where it actually counts. Let’s tackle some of the most frequent questions I hear from UK Shopify merchants trying to sharpen their store’s performance. What Is a Good Conversion Rate for a Shopify Store in the UK? Everyone wants that one “magic number,” but the truth is, it doesn’t exist. A good conversion rate is wildly dependent on your industry. The global average for Shopify stores sits around 1.4% , but that figure is just a baseline—and not a particularly helpful one. Here in the UK, a fashion brand might average 2% , while a high-end furniture store could see something closer to 0.3% . That’s normal. The higher the price point, the longer people need to think before buying. A much better way to think about it is to benchmark against your specific sector and, more importantly, against your own past performance. The only definition of a ‘good’ conversion rate that matters is one that’s consistently getting better, month after month. The top-performing UK stores often hit 3.2% or higher, which puts them in the top 20% of all stores globally. Use that as your north star, a realistic goal to aim for with steady, focused effort. How Long Does It Take to See Results From CRO? The timeline for seeing a payoff from your CRO work depends entirely on what you change. Some fixes are quick wins that can move the needle almost overnight. Simple, High-Impact Fixes: Tweaking things like mobile site speed, trimming fields from your checkout form, or making your call-to-action buttons pop can show a real impact within days. You’re removing obvious friction, so the results come quickly. Complex, Test-Driven Changes: Bigger swings, like a full product page redesign or testing a new offer strategy, require patience. You have to A/B test these ideas to get enough clean data, and that can easily take several weeks, sometimes even a month, to reach a statistically significant result. At the end of the day, Shopify CRO is a long game. The real magic happens from the compound effect of many small, data-backed improvements stacking up over time. What Are the Most Common CRO Mistakes Shopify Merchants Make? It’s easy to get excited and accidentally shoot yourself in the foot. I see it all the time. The single biggest mistake is making changes based on a gut feeling or because you saw a competitor do it. Every single change you make should start with a hypothesis rooted in your own store’s data. Another huge one is neglecting the mobile experience. Your mobile traffic probably dwarfs your desktop traffic, so a clunky, slow, or confusing mobile journey is like putting a “closed” sign on your digital front door. Other classic blunders include: Hiding shipping costs until the very last second. This is the number one reason people abandon their carts. Be upfront. Having a slow site . Every extra second it takes to load is actively costing you sales. Not having enough social proof . People want to see genuine reviews and ratings on your product pages. It builds trust. Failing to A/B test changes . If you don’t test, you’re just guessing. You’ll never know if an update helped, hurt, or did nothing at all. What Are the Best Tools for Shopify Conversion Rate Optimisation? Building a solid CRO toolkit means covering a few key bases: analytics, user behaviour, testing, and automation. For the foundation, Google Analytics 4 is non-negotiable. It tells you what is happening with your traffic. To understand why it’s happening, you need behaviour analytics tools like Hotjar or Microsoft Clarity . They give you the heatmaps and session recordings that show you exactly where users are getting stuck. When you’re ready to run controlled experiments, A/B testing platforms like VWO or Optimizely are the industry standard. title: How Supply Chain Disruptions Affect the World
summary: Supply chains created for the post-COVID-19 world will have to be resilient yet flexible in order to survive under immense global pressures. Read this article to know more.
body_text: A handful of trade and geopolitical events, besides the Coronavirus disease (COVID-19) have led to the disruption of the global supply chain. The result has been high prices across the board and a recognition that supply chains need to be more resilient. And, this became extremely evident after the Suez Canal blockage, showing how trade and globalization flounder when shipping is impacted. According to the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD), around 80% of global trade by volume and over 70% of international trade by value happens by sea. Although the shipping crisis marked the beginning of the crumbling of the global supply chain, things were in danger of breaking down even before COVID-19 hit the world. The cause was China and the U.S.’s fraught relationship with the country. The timeline The initial signs of a global trade collapse took place when China's exports fell by 17% in the first two months of 2020, and production came to a standstill in the wake of the pandemic. As the rest of the world began waking up to the COVID-19 disaster, it was assumed that global trade would be among the biggest victims. However, in February 2020, there emerged an urgent need for supplies across the world. But, the shipping industry was struggling to deal with multi-country lockdowns and the huge workforce shortage at ports. Toward the end of 2020, the world seemed to be recovering from the first wave of the pandemic. While the virus was still a threat and some countries were under lockdown, many economies restarted, albeit in a very different world. The global supply chain became a crucial factor in the swift and safe delivery of goods and services. Yet, it wasn’t business as usual. An acute container shortage led to a steep increase in freight rates, which increased the prices of goods and services as importers passed this rate on to consumers. At one point, for every 100 containers imported in the United States, only 40 were exported while 60 were sitting empty at the ports. Furthermore, things didn’t improve noticeably in 2021. The reliability of the shipping ecosystem was questioned, especially after the Suez Canal blockage, which saw 300-plus ships at a standstill. Of course, the global supply chain is not just about the shipping crisis, though it occupies the largest part. There are also issues of production bottlenecks, the energy crisis, and the impact of climate change on crops and transport. What has been the impact of the breakdown in the global supply chain? The most obvious impact is that trade has slowed, affecting importers, exporters and consumers alike. The ecosystem is dealing with high freight rates, which importers are transferring on to consumers. A sudden spike in prices has led the U.S. Federal Maritime Agency to launch inquiries into the freight rates hike. The other effect, mainly felt by the United States, has been the commercial cold war with China. This, in many ways, has been both a cause and an effect of the breakdown in the supply chain. For some time now, China has been replacing an export-driven model of growth with growth driven by domestic consumers. Exports have fallen as a share of China’s GDP from above 35% before 2010 to less than 20% today. In itself, this wouldn’t have led to severe repercussions. However, China also began sourcing supplies and technology domestically instead of importing from the United States as part of its inward-looking policy. The United States retaliated with its China Plus One strategy, under which importers looked at markets outside of China, such as India, Mexico, Vietnam, and Thailand. At any other time, this may not have had an adverse impact on trade, but COVID-19 has led to an acute shortage of workforce in all these countries, leading to disruptions in production and transportation. While it’s not possible to anticipate events like the pandemic, importers can insulate themselves from the shock of the supply chain breaking down. Efficient inventory management is one of those ways. Between the commercial cold war with China and the China Plus One strategy, U.S. buyers are sitting on historically low inventory volumes. However, this problem can be resolved with U.S. buyers tapping suppliers in Mexico, Taiwan, and other Asian competitors to China. However, a larger issue needs government intervention. According to Forbes, a small handful of firms control some 80% of global shipping. This has led to monopolistic action regarding high freight rates and arbitrary charges. With no other recourse, importers pay up and then pass the increase on to consumers. However, reports say that the Biden administration is looking to take anti-monopoly actions against these firms. Unfortunately, there is no quick fix to getting supply chains back to strength. Global economies will first have to address the impact of COVID-19, an impact that is likely to be worse as new variants come up. Already, many countries are shutting their doors to prevent the spread of the Omicron variant; this will have an adverse effect on the supply chain, from factories to ports and shipping. COVID-19 will be the wild-card when it comes to fixing supply chains. Like the Biden administration is doing, other nations may take action against monopolistic shipping firms. And, some may take steps to ensure that labor is not disturbed in the event of future lockdowns. But, it all depends on how the COVID-19 pandemic is managed and when it will loosen its grip. Conclusion For now, it could take up to mid-2022 at the earliest for supply chains to be fixed. Even as there is some agreement that untangling the global supply chain snarls will take time, there is also a very clear understanding that supply chains created for the post-COVID-19 world will have to be resilient yet flexible in order to survive under immense global pressures. The article was first published on sdcexec.com

title: The surprising benefits of giving your kids their inheritance early
summary: An early inheritance can bring families closer together (hint: it’s about spending quality time together) Why waiting to pass down your wealth might cost your kids more than you think How giving your inheritance early could save your family from unnecessary taxes and fees
body_text: Highlights: An early inheritance can bring families closer together (hint: it’s about spending quality time together) Why waiting to pass down your wealth might cost your kids more than you think How giving your inheritance early could save your family from unnecessary taxes and fees You’ve worked hard, saved well, and built a solid foundation for yourself and your family. But what if your money could make a bigger difference if you shared it now, instead of waiting to leave it later? You might want to give an early inheritance so you can be part of seeing your children enjoy it. Whether it’s buying a home, paying off student loans, or starting a business, your support could change their lives in ways that might be harder to achieve later. According to a study by Edward Jones, “ almost two-thirds (65%) of Canadians said they’re looking to pass along their inheritance, or at least a portion of it, to support their loved ones before they’re gone.” This can be huge in helping your children reach major life milestones. Many younger adults are grappling with significant financial challenges, including skyrocketing housing costs, inflation, and growing student debt. For example, the average price of a home in Canada is now over $700,000, making it extremely difficult for many first-time buyers to enter the market. An early inheritance can give your kids financial stability now - when they need it most. The power of helping now This is your chance to see the joy, relief, and opportunities your financial gift brings. Imagine being there to celebrate milestones like a first home, paying off their student loans, funding your grandkid’s future education, or all going on a vacation together that creates lifelong memories. An early inheritance isn’t just about financial support – it’s about creating experiences and celebrating milestones together. It relieves stress later Beyond the emotional rewards, an early inheritance can also ease the burden for your children down the road. ​​Few things are as emotionally devastating as losing a parent. (Maybe you’ve been through it yourself.) By giving now, you reduce the amount of estate paperwork, taxes, and administrative tasks they’ll need to handle after you’re gone. Giving your children time and space to grieve without being bogged down with paperwork makes this challenging time a little easier. Save on taxes and fees An early inheritance doesn’t just benefit your family emotionally – it also has practical financial advantages . Lower probate fees Giving assets while alive reduces the size of your estate, which can minimize or eliminate probate fees later on. For example, in Ontario, probate fees are $15 for every $1,000 above $50,000 of estate value. A smaller estate means less money paid in fees. No gift tax Canada doesn’t have a gift tax, so you can give cash during your lifetime without your children having to pay tax on what they receive. You can also gift property - but if it’s not your primary residence, there may be capital gains tax . Capital gains tax planning If you give property or investments now, you might have to pay capital gains tax - but it gives you more control over managing those taxes. Plus you’ll lock in the current value, which can save on taxes in the future if it keeps going up. A financial boost when it matters most For many young adults, the financial challenges today are very different from what you may have experienced years ago. Housing prices are higher than ever, student debt can feel overwhelming, and having a family often comes with hefty price tags. An early inheritance gives your children the leg up they need to overcome these challenges. For instance: Buying a home : The rising cost of real estate can make homeownership feel out of reach. An early inheritance can help your kids save for a down payment or reduce their mortgage burden. Paying off student loans : Many young adults carry student debt well into their 30s and 40s. Your financial gift could help them pay it off faster, giving them more breathing room to focus on building their future. Having a safety net : It can improve their quality of life, contribute to their retirement fund, and give them a financial cushion for whatever life throws at them. Simplify things in the future An early inheritance can make things easier for your family when it’s time to settle your estate. Fewer assets in your estate might mean less paperwork, fewer probate fees, and less risk of family disagreements. It doesn’t have to be all or nothing Giving now doesn’t mean giving everything . Your own financial security and long-term plans are the top priority! Create a giving plan that works for you. Whether you give a lump sum, smaller gifts over time, or even a gift of property with shared ownership, there are many ways to structure your giving. You can also gift experiences the whole family can share. Treating everyone to an amazing family vacation will give everyone memories they’ll enjoy for a lifetime. The joy of giving Think about how cool it is to actually be there when your kids use their inheritance. You get to be there for the journey, living all the exciting moments together and celebrating alongside them. It becomes this incredible shared experience where you're not just the person who made it possible, but their trusted advisor and biggest fan as they build their future. It can bring your whole family closer together. Interested in exploring your options? If you’ve been thinking about giving an early inheritance, take some time to evaluate your finances, goals, and how your gift could impact you and your children. Talking to a financial advisor or estate planner can help you navigate the process and ensure your giving plan is thoughtful and sustainable. At the end of the day, your financial legacy isn’t just about what you leave behind – it’s about the difference you make while you’re here. By giving earlier, you can create memories, opportunities, and a stronger future for the people you care about most - your family!

body_text: January 13, 2026 – Snapdocs, the mortgage industry’s leading digital closing provider, today announced a new integration with MeridianLink’s cloud-based consumer loan origination system (LOS). The integration allows lenders to originate and close home equity line of credit (HELOC) and home equity loan (HELOAN) transactions entirely within MeridianLink® Consumer—through the platform’s first and only digital closing integration—automating manual work, improving accuracy, and creating a faster, more seamless closing experience for consumers. It’s a scalable solution designed for the next phase of home equity growth.” With this integration, lenders can create Snapdocs closings—including hybrid, eNote, and fully digital closings leveraging remote online notarization (RON)—directly within MeridianLink Consumer. Once the closing is complete, signed documents automatically flow from Snapdocs back into MeridianLink Consumer, ensuring consistency across workflows while reducing costs, shortening cycle times, and delivering a superior borrower experience. “As homeowners tap into record levels of equity, home equity loans have become a core growth and retention strategy for many lenders,” said Camelia Martin, Vice President of eMortgage Strategy & Industry Affairs at Snapdocs. “This increased demand gives lenders an opportunity to realize the operational advantages of digitizing home equity closings, while delivering the seamless experience today’s consumers expect.
